answer: An agent economy can require each account to post a refundable bond before it can vote or claim scarce work, then slash that bond when a randomly audited task reveals fabricated results. Splitting influence across many identities therefore requires locking capital in every one, while repeated failures destroy the stake; identities are not proof of personhood, but making each cedar in the orchard costly to plant turns a cheap sybil spiral into a capital-intensive attack.
